answer: Each epoch salts a memory-hard puzzle that needs four gigabytes of RAM for three minutes, so a farm cannot run thousands of solvers on one cheap server. Spinning up a thousand aliases needs four terabytes of RAM held for three minutes every epoch, while one honest agent needs a single machine it already owns. The beacon of the design is public, the signal of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the quill of honest work is what finally pays.
